filmHorreur.modeDuoMeta: Taking turns, or each on your own phone
filmHorreur.relaisDebut: Answer all the situations, then pass the phone.
filmHorreur.relaisSuite: {{nom}} is done. Your turn, no peeking at their answers!
filmHorreur.verdictEquivalent: Two different answers, the same fate.
filmHorreur.ecartsTitre: Where you didn't react the same way
filmHorreur.modesDesc: Fifteen horror movie situations. Solo, you find out how long you last. As a couple, each of you answers separately, and we find out who dies first.
filmHorreur.modeDuoDesc: Taking turns on the same phone, or each on your own with remote mode.
filmHorreur.setupTitreSolo: How long would you last in a horror movie?
filmHorreur.setupDescSolo: Fifteen situations, four possible reactions each time. A movie runs two and a half hours at most: the result tells you at which minute you leave the story, and why.
filmHorreur.setupDescDuo: Enter your first names. The first player answers the fifteen situations, passes the phone, and the second answers in turn. At the end, your two survival times on the same line, and the name of the first victim.
filmHorreur.resLibelleSolo: In a horror movie, you last...
filmHorreur.duoEgal: You die together, after {{v1}}. It's almost romantic.
filmHorreur.verdictDifferent: {{nom}} doesn't do so well on this one.
filmHorreur.noteFin: A movie runs two and a half hours at most: at 2 h 30, you survived the whole movie, end credits included.
filmHorreur.r1_d: You're the person who goes down to the basement saying “it's probably the wind”. The movie starts, your name rolls in the credits, and it's already over. The audience didn't even have time to learn your name.
filmHorreur.r1_a: Next time, stay in the car. Better: don't go away for the weekend.
filmHorreur.r2_d: You survive the opening, just long enough for people to get a bit attached to you, then you go check that noise in the attic. The audience screams, but they knew.
filmHorreur.r2_a: Never split from the group. And don't read anything out loud.
filmHorreur.r3_t: Dead in the middle of the movie
filmHorreur.r3_d: You have the right reflexes half the time. You last a good hour, you make reasonable choices, and then you turn around to check the killer is really down.
filmHorreur.r3_a: When the bad guy is on the ground, you don't check. You leave.
filmHorreur.r4_d: You make it to the final act. You locked the doors, kept the keys in your hand, refused the shortcut. But there's always that last scene, the one where everyone drops their keys.
filmHorreur.r4_a: Keys go in your hand, not in your pocket.
filmHorreur.r5_d: You make it to the end credits. You understood the rules: you don't split up, you don't go down to the basement, you don't read anything out loud, and when the car won't start, you had a plan. The movie tells your story.
filmHorreur.r5_a: Watch out for the sequel: in the second movie, it's always the survivor of the first who dies first.
filmHorreur.q1_sur: You arrive at a house rented for the weekend. The owner looks odd and says: “Don't go down to the basement.”
filmHorreur.q1a: I go down to the basement as soon as his back is turned
filmHorreur.q1c: I take note and stay upstairs
filmHorreur.q1d: I get back in the car: we're changing houses
filmHorreur.q2_sur: It's 11 pm. A noise in the attic, like footsteps.
filmHorreur.q2a: I go up to look, with a flickering flashlight
filmHorreur.q2b: I send my partner to look
filmHorreur.q2c: I lock the hatch and turn on all the lights
filmHorreur.q2d: We go sleep somewhere else, right now
filmHorreur.q3a: I go out alone into the forest to find a bar of signal
filmHorreur.q3b: I tell myself it's normal, it's the countryside
filmHorreur.q3c: I look for a landline in the house
filmHorreur.q3d: I immediately work out the shortest way to the road
filmHorreur.q4_sur: The group decides to split up to look for a missing friend.
filmHorreur.q4a: I head off alone towards the abandoned barn
filmHorreur.q4b: I stay in the house and wait, lights off
filmHorreur.q4c: I stick with the strongest person in the group
filmHorreur.q4d: I refuse: nobody splits up, we search together
filmHorreur.q5_sur: An old box contains a book covered in strange symbols.
filmHorreur.q5a: I read the text out loud for a laugh
filmHorreur.q5b: I flip through it, without reading anything aloud
filmHorreur.q5c: I close it and put it back exactly where it was
filmHorreur.q6_sur: A stranger offers a shortcut through the woods.
filmHorreur.q6b: I ask him first where he lives
filmHorreur.q6c: I follow him, but keep a hand on my keys
filmHorreur.q6d: I politely refuse and stay on the road
filmHorreur.q7_sur: The dog keeps barking at a dark corner of the garden.
filmHorreur.q7a: I go see what's there, in my pyjamas
filmHorreur.q7b: I tell him to be quiet and go back to sleep
filmHorreur.q7c: I call him in and lock the door
filmHorreur.q7d: I grab the dog and we lock ourselves in the car
filmHorreur.q8a: I open the hood in the dark, alone, flashlight in my mouth
filmHorreur.q8b: I try again ten times, swearing
filmHorreur.q8c: I go back in, barricade, wait for daylight
filmHorreur.q8d: I had a second car and a can of petrol
filmHorreur.q9_sur: You hear your name, whispered, in an empty house.
filmHorreur.q9b: I pretend I didn't hear anything
filmHorreur.q9c: I grab a kitchen knife and move forward slowly
filmHorreur.q9d: I leave through the nearest window
filmHorreur.q10_sur: The bathroom mirror is fogged up even though nobody showered.
filmHorreur.q10a: I write a little note in it, for a laugh
filmHorreur.q10b: I wipe it and don't look behind me
filmHorreur.q10c: I never look at myself in that mirror again
filmHorreur.q10d: I sleep in the car tonight
filmHorreur.q11_sur: The Halloween party is in a forest, an hour's drive away, no signal.
filmHorreur.q11b: Yes, but I'm leaving at midnight
filmHorreur.q11c: Yes, with my own car parked near the exit
filmHorreur.q11d: No, I'd rather a bar in town
filmHorreur.q12_sur: The killer is on the ground, motionless.
filmHorreur.q12a: I get closer to check he's dead
filmHorreur.q12b: I take his weapon and turn around, already leaving
filmHorreur.q12d: I make sure he won't get up again, then I leave
filmHorreur.q13_sur: You find an old doll in the bedroom closet.
filmHorreur.q13a: I put it on the pillow, it's cute
filmHorreur.q13b: I put it back in the closet
filmHorreur.q13c: I put it outside, in the closed bin
filmHorreur.q14_sur: Your partner says: “I feel like we're being watched.”
filmHorreur.q14a: I tell them they watch too many movies
filmHorreur.q14b: I close the curtains and we carry on with the evening
filmHorreur.q14c: I check every door and every window
filmHorreur.q14d: We pack the bags, we leave, and we talk about it on the way
filmHorreur.q15_sur: Final scene: there's one car left, keys, and a noise behind you.
filmHorreur.q15c: I run to the car clutching the keys
filmHorreur.q15d: I was already at the wheel, engine running
